recap.narration_text: Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: driver. seat. distraction. No preparation can eliminate every driving hazard, but recognizing hazards helps a driver respond. Before departure, check the travel path, adjust the seat and mirrors, buckle occupants and remove distractions. Visual distraction diverts the eyes, manual distraction occupies the hands and cognitive distraction diverts attention.

Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: collision. collision. vehicle. Store loose objects in the trunk when possible so they are less likely to strike occupants in a collision. The guide recommends keeping writing materials, insurance details and emergency supplies in a collision kit. Know which braking system the vehicle has; the owner’s manual can identify anti-lock equipment.

Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: brakes. safe. neutral. During a tire blowout, hold the wheel firmly and avoid slamming on the brakes. After a blowout, keep the vehicle controlled as it slows, then brake gently and stop in a safe place. If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road and shift into neutral.

Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: water. safe. police. The guide’s water-escape cue POGO means releasing belts, opening windows and getting out. After a collision involving injury, death or damage, stop when safe and identify yourself rather than leaving the scene. Request police assistance after a collision and an ambulance when needed.
